speak.title: Role-play: how should the museum tell this story?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your museum wants a display about the Siberian tomb. You like the headline 'People Got High 2,800 Years Ago'. It will bring in visitors. Explain why, and listen to your colleague's worries.

b.text: You worked on the study. The evidence is real, but it leaves many questions open. Explain what the hair and seeds can show and what they can't. Suggest a better headline and try to agree.

phrases: I'd like a headline that grabs people's attention.
That's true, but it isn't the whole story.
We can't say that for certain.
The hair shows exposure, not how often people used it.
How about a title that's honest and still interesting?
I think we can agree on that.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what headline did you agree on, and why?
